title: Bug hunt: fuzzing a codec
hints: A fuzz test is `func FuzzX(f *testing.F)`: call `f.Add(seed)` for each seed, then `f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, s string) { ... })`. Inside, don't compare with hand-written answers — check a **property** that holds for every input, like `Decode(Encode(s)) == s`.

Each bug name tells you which seed exposes it: a run of 12 of the same rune (two-digit count), `"aAAa"` (case), `"héé"` or `"日本日本"` (multi-byte), `"::a:"` (the separator as text), and any non-empty string (the last run). For the `Decode` fuzz test, seed broken inputs such as `"3:"` and `"1:\xff"`; if `Decode` panics, the test fails on its own.

The zero-count bug produces a valid-looking result, so no round-trip property can see it — that is what the table test is for: `for _, in := range []string{"a", ":a", "3:", "0:a", "x:a", "2:a3"} { if _, err := Decode(in); !errors.Is(err, ErrMalformed) { t.Errorf(...) } }`. Finish with `func ExampleEncode() { fmt.Println(Encode("aaab")) // Output: 3:a1:b }` and `func BenchmarkEncode(b *testing.B) { s := strings.Repeat("aaab", 100); for b.Loop() { Encode(s) } }`.
